falsifier: the arm's reports hold no crossing with decided false
hypothesis: the archived after arm of #1075 (Baseline 6bff717, analysis mode) shows what a lane does with an undecidable crossing and how the critic splits drafts on one, so both halves can be read offline
intervention: counted decided false in every boundary_crossings block of the arm's 13 reports, of all 253 archived reports, of the 254 archived models in evals/runs, and of today's corpus model.json files; then validated the raw extraction emissions of 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-19 through today's SystemModel and counted undecidable crossings. Arm: 0 of the 29 flows the research note simulates as undecidable were undecidable at run time; all 29 were decided on an assumed endpoint. All archived reports: 0 undecidable crossings. Today's corpus models: 0 undecidable of 52 crossings, 34 decided on an assumed endpoint. Extraction emissions, naming-rule r1 to r3 (the latest): 179 undecidable of 222 crossings over 38 valid extractions, 154 unplaced elements; placement-rule after arm 305 of 386; before arm 205 of 331. So an analysis-mode run, which reads the blessed model, cannot contain an undecidable crossing, while an end-to-end run meets one on about four crossings in five
reconsider_when: the corpus models stop placing components the sources never place, or an end-to-end run on the current prompts is archived
scope: STRIDE and ASVS alike, because the crossing is derived from the System Model; 13 tuned cases; extraction counts from luna emissions replayed through today's validation, so they measure what extraction emits, not what a lane does with it; no lane or critic output exists for an undecidable crossing, so neither half of #1075 is measured
signature: an undecidable crossing never reaches a lane in an analysis-mode run

falsifier: no two credential-family drafts in the archived Baselines share a key
hypothesis: produced STRIDE drafts collide on one claim identity (lane, verb, folded place) because they use two credentials at one place, as #1438 records for one reference pair
intervention: grouped every STRIDE draft of the four archived Baselines (2198870, 6bff717, d3f1898, d4edd64; 13 cases each) by category, verb and endpoint_targets, before the critic, and read every group holding two drafts. Keys by family: disclosure 258, integrity 207, identity 132, availability 82, attribution 84, authorization 71, credential 56. Groups with two drafts: 11 (identity 7, integrity 2, authorization 1, availability 1, credential 0). Every group holds two different findings. 5 of 11 are impersonate in opposite directions on one flow: a fake server to the client against a fake client to the server (case 09 in three Baselines, case 01, case 10). 6 of 11 differ by access path or channel (a leaked password against an offline copy; MQTT floods against Pub/Sub floods; an over-broad token against a retained one; cross-origin requests against a WebSocket handshake, twice in case 13). In 9 of 11 the critic gave the two drafts different verdicts, and both reached the report
reconsider_when: the identity rule versions, the verb vocabulary changes, or a sweep shows a credential pair colliding
scope: STRIDE, 13 tuned cases, four Baselines, analysis mode; drafts before the critic; one agent's reading of the 11 groups. A flow-derived direction (ADR 0031) would not separate the 5 impersonation pairs, because both drafts of a pair cite the same flow; what separates them is which side is impersonated, which no claim field carries
signature: two different findings share one claim identity in a run

falsifier: a duplicate rejection in the archive drops a draft that states a different finding, or a #890 different ruling falls on a same-key pair
hypothesis: the same-key collisions of E2 cost nothing, because the critic keeps both drafts of a pair and the scorer is not misled
intervention: read the critic's rejection reasons for the 11 E2 pairs; matched each paired draft to its Baseline's reference claims at the Baseline's own commit with endpoint_subset and same_action; looked the pairs up in the #890 ballot (QA-2026-09-26-01/E1-must-find-matches-by-meaning.csv); read every duplicate rejection in every archived report. Four Baselines: all 3 STRIDE duplicate rejections fall on E2 pairs (cases 02, 08, 13). In every pair both drafts match the same one reference. In 6bff717, case 02 ref 10 (the MQTT connection flood) and case 13 ref 1 (the WebSocket handshake) lost the draft that stated the reference as a duplicate, and the kept draft the scorer credited was ruled different on the #890 ballot. Case 09 ref 0, also ruled different, is a same-key pair whose two drafts are a customer and a fake server. So 3 of the 12 different rulings fall on same-key pairs. Whole archive: 10 distinct duplicate rejections; by one reading each dropped a different finding: 5 opposite-direction impersonation, 3 another mechanism or path, 2 another action (one of them across two lanes)
reconsider_when: the critic's duplicate step changes, or a run shows a duplicate rejection that removed a true duplicate
scope: STRIDE; analysis mode; the 10 archived duplicate rejections and the 12 ballot rows; one agent's reading of what counts as a different finding, except the three ballot rows, which the maintainer ruled
signature: the critic rejects a different finding as a duplicate

falsifier: the answered facts are cited in nearly every lane, or findings move in lanes no answered fact touches
hypothesis: a follow-up that reran only the lanes holding a finding that cites an answered fact, and reused the other lanes' drafts, would skip a material share of lane calls and lose no moved finding
intervention: for the five withheld-and-answered report pairs of 20260928T-withheld-01 (case 01, three answered authentication facts), marked a lane targeted where a finding of the withheld report cites an answered fact in its grounds or open facts, then matched the reports with report_changes. Targeted lanes: 26 of 30 (5, 6, 5, 5 and 5 of 6). Findings that moved (new, changed or gone): 84, of which 4 moved in an untargeted lane (0, 0, 1, 0, 3)
reconsider_when: a real owner's answers (#1286) touch a few lanes of a large selection, or a selection runs many frameworks
scope: STRIDE, case 01 only, three answered facts, five pairs; lane-level reuse only, because a lane writes its findings together; the critic would still rule every draft
signature: a follow-up runs every lane again for answers that touch a few
